ideas.risks: A positive result may need assumptions not present in the atlas source. A finite-cell abstraction could miss continuous or adaptive queries, and a negative LP certificate may only rule out one-step public filters.
ideas.summary: Model a public transcript as a finite partition with variables for each cell's mass, comparator posterior error, and current predictor behavior. Optimize over all public nonnegative filters and sign relabelings to decide whether excess risk over a comparator ever forces a query with comparator error below gamma. Include sign-specific cells, not just aggregate agreement or mistake filters.
ideas.title: Observable Residual Minimax LP
ideas.why_promising: This directly tests the weakest missing step in residual-forcing proofs and could produce either a usable low-noise-query lemma or a crisp finite counterexample explaining why no public residual method can work.

ideas.risks: The oracle may satisfy the guarantee by returning an anchor hypothesis and ignoring the small target perturbation. Suitable public anchors may not exist for arbitrary C, and fixed additive slack may swamp any epsilon-scale information.
ideas.summary: Study label-doping queries where the conditional label mean is a mixture of a known public anchor signal and the original target labels. Vary the mixing weight and reweighting to see whether a constant-additive correlation oracle can be converted into an epsilon-accurate optimizer for the original correlation objective, or prove this is impossible without strong anchor structure.
ideas.title: Anchor Doping For Support-Function Refinement
ideas.why_promising: It attacks the hard-band silence without hidden clean transcripts. A success would give a new positive route; a failure could become a clean black-box obstruction to upgrading fixed additive optimization.

ideas.risks: The public-posterior obstruction suggests the needed filter may require information about the hidden comparator. The dual object may depend on c and be nonconstructive, or may only give comparator error just below gamma with no polynomial margin.
ideas.summary: Try to prove a hard-core or dense-model decomposition: if the current final classifier is more than epsilon above OPT_C, then a minimax-selected public distribution over filters/relabelings contains a query where a near-optimal comparator has error at most gamma minus poly(epsilon). Avoid the known high-loss and mistake-residual failures by optimizing over a richer public filter family.
ideas.title: Hard-Core Low-OPT Chunk Lemma
ideas.why_promising: Such a lemma would turn the fixed weak learner into a fully polynomial booster and would conceptually replace da Cunha-style hidden clean enumeration with a dual certificate.

ideas.risks: Known approximation algorithms may be distribution-specific, margin-dependent, or proper only. Known hardness may not apply to arbitrary improper predictors. The weak guarantee must hold for every joint distribution, not just planted noise models.
ideas.summary: Search for represented classes with an efficient distribution-free algorithm achieving error at most a*OPT + epsilon, while OPT+epsilon improper agnostic learning is hard. For gamma with a*gamma <= 1/2, this would imply a fixed OPT+beta weak learner by combining the approximation algorithm below gamma with constants above gamma. Audit halfspaces, polynomial threshold functions, intersections, sparse parities, and related classes under this exact checklist.
ideas.title: Constant-Factor Weak, PTAS-Hard Classes
ideas.why_promising: This converts existing approximation-versus-PTAS gaps into the desired separation template and avoids the classical decoding/improper-learning mismatch.

ideas.risks: Low-noise distribution-free weak learning may be as hard as moderate-noise prediction. Improper prediction may be easier than message recovery. Arbitrary coordinate marginals may break standard decoding or list-decoding algorithms.
ideas.summary: Pick one succinct huge-domain code or pseudorandom family and test the strict separation checklist: efficient weighted/soft weak learning whenever OPT_C < gamma under arbitrary marginals, but sample-access improper RCN prediction hardness at some eta > gamma. Work through domain representation, evaluation, and the table-learning escape explicitly.
ideas.title: Succinct RCN Prediction Candidate
ideas.why_promising: The polynomial-domain code route is blocked, but a succinct-domain sample-access prediction hardness assumption remains one of the few credible negative templates.

ideas.risks: Fingerprinting controls only the current query marginal, not future hidden clean slices. A can hide arbitrary bits off support or in semantically equivalent hypotheses. Dual VC can remain large despite short empirical fingerprints.
ideas.summary: Try to regularize an arbitrary fixed-slack learner A by repeated fresh runs, validation on the query distribution, prediction fingerprinting on an independent unlabeled sample, and canonical representative selection. Prove or refute that the resulting learner has bounded effective range, stability, compression, or dual VC sufficient for the da Cunha route.
ideas.title: Canonicalize The Weak Learner
ideas.why_promising: If successful, it removes the controlled-range assumption from the strongest positive near miss. If impossible, an explicit bit-encoding weak learner would justify treating controlled range as a genuine extra hypothesis.

ideas.risks: Even a tractable final selector would not solve hidden-clean bag generation or clean-slice population transfer. The exact da Cunha proof may rely on enumerated clean samples before the vote-selection step.
ideas.summary: Extract the exact final vote class in the da Cunha proof: sparse signed majority, nonnegative convex vote, bounded T-wise vote, or unrestricted threshold over a bag. For each version, decide whether selection is polynomial via enumeration, LP/surrogate with a calibration theorem, or whether coordinate-bag reductions make it as hard as agnostic halfspace learning.
ideas.title: Exact Vote Selector Stress Test
ideas.why_promising: This isolates one bottleneck that can be studied independently and could sharpen the conditional theorem into the weakest possible selector assumption.

ideas.risks: The light-mass remainder may still contain the whole hard problem. The decomposition may not respect C or the adaptive distributions used by A. Heavy-atom learning helps lower bounds more than it helps the positive route.
ideas.summary: Split D_X into empirically heavy atoms and a high-min-entropy remainder. Learn heavy atoms by repeated-label/table-style prediction, then formulate smooth public-filter or clean-certificate barriers only on the light part. Check whether this removes the repeated-coordinate denoising and point-mass loopholes in restricted lower-bound models.
ideas.title: Heavy-Atom Light-Tail Split
ideas.why_promising: Many failed barriers break on spikes, empirical supports, or repeated-coordinate denoising. This decomposition could make future oracle barriers precise without overclaiming.
